title: Kiosk scan rejection
lede: A blocked candidate is rejected at scan time, so the visible cart remains a trustworthy count of accepted items.

stats.n: Only items that pass the candidate availability check enter the cart/count
The holder, item, deadline, and not-added result are visible together

sections.heading: Checkout scan stage
sections.note: Same conflicted candidate and iPad Air 11-inch (M4) simulator viewport. Before is the inspected pre-rejection state from the existing availability-conflicts capture; after is the fresh post-rejection fixture state from the verified Debug build.

pairs.title: When the FX3 is already reserved
pairs.sub: The cart count should describe accepted items, not every barcode that passed through the scanner.
pairs.beforeCap: The reserved FX3 is already staged, so the cart says 4 items even though the availability banner says checkout is blocked.
pairs.afterCap: The FX3 is absent, the cart says 2 items, and the rejection banner keeps Erik Role, the deadline, and the explicit not-added outcome together.

changes.h: A blocking scan no longer looks accepted
changes.was: The scan endpoint could succeed and the client staged the item before the future reservation conflict was known, leaving a misleading cart count and a blocked completion step.
changes.now: Checkout serializes candidates and preflights the candidate cart before insertion; a blocking reservation, checkout, unavailable-asset, or bulk-shortage result is rejected and never increments the visible count.

changes.h: Failure feedback works in the assembly line
changes.was: The operator had to notice a visual error banner or haptic while continuing through a rapid scan sequence.
changes.now: Rejected, failed, and duplicate feedback retains the visual, haptic, and VoiceOver announcement and adds a short procedural failure cue; successful scans and non-blocking warnings stay quiet.

verification: Focused source contracts: 17/17 passing across the new rejection/sound suite and the existing Kiosk availability, recovery, numbered-battery, and pickup contracts.
Native gates: WisconsinKiosk Debug and Release builds pass for the iPad Air 11-inch (M4), iOS 26.5 simulator; project parity, drift, iOS gap audits, and diff checks pass.
Visual: both PNGs were inspected after installing the fresh Debug build; the post-rejection capture shows only admitted items in the cart and the named rejection message.
Audio boundary: the procedural cue is compile-wired and failure-only by source contract; actual speaker loudness and scanner-floor audibility remain a physical-iPad gate.
notes: This is local source/build/simulator proof only. The final server availability check and transactional completion guard remain authoritative, and no API, schema, permission, allocation, audit, or custody semantics changed.

The before image is the previously captured, inspected pre-rejection output for the same availability-conflict candidate and viewport. The after image uses the dedicated post-rejection fixture state so the expected absence from the cart is directly visible rather than reconstructed by hand.
Deployment and managed-iPad speaker/scanner replay are still open; the simulator cannot prove a physical sounder output.
